evidence.decision: Chooses a recurring useful function instead of merely opening the app, and keeps first and secondary press meanings predictable rather than assigning arbitrary destructive behavior.
evidence.artifact: Requires an Action label, press-state/result contract, and fallback entry route; these can directly drive a shortcut or device interaction design.
evidence.transformation: The field-notes example changes Open Field Notes plus unrelated save/delete presses into Record Waypoint with stable repeated behavior and explicit destructive UI.
evidence.verification: Checks unexpected destruction, repeated-press termination and lost task context, while explicitly leaving device-specific press and feedback behavior for hardware execution.
evidence.applicability: Separates iPhone snippet/Live Activity context from Watch first and memorable secondary actions, including the supported Action-plus-side pause exception rather than imposing one mapping everywhere.
evidence.handoffs: Sends shared shortcut work to Siri and wrist-down feedback to Always On only when those features are involved.
evidence.distinctiveness: The three-word present-tense label, essential function selection, repeated-press policy and context-preserving result make this an Action button procedure rather than a generic controls checklist.
